reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus in Pottawattamie County that it established in 2007 and has expanded continuously since, anchored by over $20 billion in cumulative Iowa investment and a $7 billion expansion announced for the Council Bluffs site itself. The campus's individual building power consumption is not published, so its exact contribution to Google's footprint cannot be read from Google's own disclosure. Iowa has 52 mapped data center facilities total, of which only 2 publish power figures; this campus ranks third among published capacity in the state, but that ranking reflects the scarcity of disclosure rather than dominance of scale.

The regional power picture shows Google has tied long-term growth at Council Bluffs to restarting the Duane Arnold nuclear plant via a NextEra Energy agreement, indicating the campus's expansion is constrained by power availability rather than real estate. Google's parallel $7 billion Cedar Rapids build signals that Council Bluffs alone cannot absorb the compute Google intends to deploy in Iowa, a pattern consistent with grid constraints limiting further growth at the Pottawattamie location.

For readers assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the absence of published per-building power figures means Council Bluffs cannot be sized against other major AI clusters. What can be read is that Google has committed to nuclear power to grow here, that it remains one of only three published-capacity sites in its state, and that it was chosen as the location for a simultaneous new campus investment, all signals of strategic importance to Google's compute footprint. The actual megawatt figure required to assess its role in national AI infrastructure remains private.
